scope: Proposition 12.3 (Circuit sparsity input) of the manuscript “Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps” (preprints/Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-and-spanning-tree-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1dd659698d3a3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 159. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Use the constants above and the available-circuit definition with the scales in Equation (12.5). Let En,N be the event that some chronological interval of length at most T, in the tested compact window, contains h pairwise ℓ-separated bad times. Along every sequence for which N −→ ∞, ne−bN −→ ∞, there is no sequence of probability laws Qn,N supported on En,N and the preselected master events just described, with e−N ≤ ρn → 0, such that Qn,N ≤ exp(κn,N )Pn, κn,N = o(N). (12.6) The same assertion holds for any fixed constant multiple of T and for sufficiently small fixed spatial neighborhoods inside the selected confinement.
